title: Buffalo Chicken Pizza
shortDescription: Blue cheese, hot sauce, crispy chicken
subtitle: Blue cheese, hot sauce, crispy chicken
description: Blue cheese, hot sauce, crispy chicken. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Toss chicken in buffalo butter
steps.instruction: Whisk hot sauce with melted butter. Toss diced chicken until coated; taste for heat — cheese and ranch mellow it. Reserve a few tablespoons of plain buffalo for after the bake.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Shred mozzarella and crumble blue cheese while the oven saturates.

steps.title: Stretch dough — light red sauce optional
steps.instruction: Stretch four 12–14 inch rounds. Buffalo Chicken is a white-ish pie: skip tomato or use only a whisper of pizza sauce if your crew expects red. Brush rims with butter from the buffalo bowl.

steps.title: Mozzarella, buffalo chicken, blue cheese
steps.instruction: Layer mozzarella, then buffalo chicken, then blue cheese crumbles. Do not drown in sauce before baking — wet buffalo pools in the center.

steps.title: Bake until cheese browns
steps.instruction: Bake 10–13 minutes until cheese bubbles and edges spot brown. Chicken is already cooked; you are setting cheese and finishing crust. Rotate once for hot spots.

steps.title: Ranch drizzle, celery, and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes. Drizzle ranch and reserved buffalo in thin lines. Scatter celery and green onions for crunch — not baked in or they go limp. Cut into 8 slices; Buffalo Chicken Pizza eats like game day on a crust.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Buffalo Chicken Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Blue cheese, hot sauce, crispy chicken. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
